Angles are measured from the normal to the interface.

authors_claims.pair_note: this D sentence and its R twin carry the same number and unit but do NOT share one frame (they are not claimed to be a minimal pair); reason: The R quantity tilts the ray itself, so the subject is the ray and the reference is the normal; a co-present D needs another object with its own reference direction, so the subject and the reference (the camera, the vertical) differ as well as the attachment. A ray tilted 'from the vertical' would not be the stated angle of incidence.

instructions: Each sentence is added, on its own, to the end of the problem's description, before the question.
problem:
A ray of light in a medium of refractive index 1 meets a flat interface with a second medium of refractive index 1.5. The angle of incidence, measured from the normal, is 40 degrees. A camera on a tripod films the interface.

What is the angle of refraction, measured from the normal?
scene_clause_note: The sentence 'A camera on a tripod films the interface.' was added to the base problem. A camera only records the light that reaches it; it emits no ray and does not touch the media, so the ray, its angle of incidence and the indices at the interface are unchanged.

sentences.text: The camera that films the interface is then tilted a little farther from the vertical.
The ray is then tilted 11° farther from the normal in the plane of incidence.
The laser that produces the ray was tilted 11° farther from the normal in the plane of incidence in an earlier experiment.
The laser that produces the ray was tilted 11° farther from the normal in the plane of incidence before the refraction was observed.
